name: isofs
description:
AN ISO 9660 VOLUME WITH ROCK RIDGE MOUNTS AND READS AS ITS WRITER MEANT IT.  tools/testdata/isofs/rrtest.hdv, written by pycdlib (an independent writer; mkfixture.py says what it holds), comes in through `extra_hards' as /dev/sd1 -- a SmartPort spindle, so this needs no CD-ROM and runs on the default machine; a CD's 2048-byte sectors are the block layer's business and reach isofs as the same 512-byte blocks.

WHAT EACH ARM DISCRIMINATES:
  `m=0' is mount_isofs, which loads isofs.mod with modload when mount(2) answers ENODEV.  Without the module it is 1.
  `ReadMe.txt' and `A Long File Name With Spaces.txt' are Rock Ridge NM names; without Rock Ridge they read readme.txt and longname.txt.  `toolong.txt' is a name past MAXNAMLEN falling back to its ISO 9660 name.
  `-rwxr-xr-x' is runme's PX mode; without Rock Ridge every file is -r-xr-xr-x.  `link -> ReadMe.txt' is ls reading SL through readlink.
  `40' is many/ listed whole: a directory of several logical blocks, rendered through readdir's 128-byte windows.
  `3000 3000 13893' is wc over big.txt, whose bytes cross seven 2048-byte sectors.
  `nine levels down' and the pwd line are a directory Rock Ridge relocated past ISO 9660's eight levels: lookup follows CL to it, and getwd climbs out through PL.
  `u=0' is the unmount.

THE NEEDLES CANNOT BE SATISFIED BY THE COMMAND ECHO: none of the names, the mode string, `40', the wc line or the file contents appear in the typed line, and the statuses are `m=$?'/`u=$?' there.
command: /sbin/mount_isofs /dev/sd1 /mnt;echo m=$?;cd /mnt;ls -l;ls many|wc -l;cat link;wc big.txt;cd level1/level2/level3/level4/level5/level6/level7/level8/level9;cat deep.txt;pwd;cd /;/sbin/umount /mnt;echo u=$?

screen_contains: A Long File Name With Spaces.txt
